children: The Bank of Japan could raise interest rates in December and again in March, with the Federal Reserve and foreign exchange rates being key, says Daiwa Securities economist Kenji Yamamoto. "If the Fed follows a December hike with another increase in January, upward pressure on U.S. interest rates and the dollar is likely to persist," he says. "Should a weaker yen increase upside inflation risks at home via higher import prices, the BOJ will have less need to wait long between rate hikes," he adds. The dollar was last trading at 159.55 yen. (megumi.fujikawa@wsj.com)
